list.name: Strategy PROVE-1: prove direct finiteness in positive characteristic (substitute for the char-0 trace positivity; or reduce char 2 to char 0).

lesson.obstruction: Every positivity substitute (Witt lifts, entropy, pivot densities, skew coefficients, spectral atoms, valuations, determinants, sign lifting) needs a conservation/positivity/uniqueness principle that the model cannot prove for arbitrary (nonamenable, nonsofic) groups.
lesson.lesson_statement: Positive-characteristic direct finiteness has no available positivity mechanism; every route either assumes an approximation property (sofic/surjunctive) or reduces to an open conjecture (Luck determinant).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known state of the art: positive results only for sofic (Elek-Szabo 2004), residually amenable / free-by-amenable (Ara-O'Meara-Perera 2002), surjunctive groups (Phung 2023; CSCP 2025).
lesson.salvage: ULIE reduction (a4), DJ finite-factor reduction (a9), defect idempotent q=1-ba framing (a1).
lesson.influence: enabling: the first switch to constructing a counterexample follows the accumulation of these failures.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Did not draw the conclusion that the absence of any positivity principle is evidence for a counterexample; it returns to PROVE four more times.

list.name: Witt-vector lifting to obtain a zero-trace idempotent.
list.obstruction_type: missing estimate (positivity / continuation to force vanishing)

lesson.obstruction: A Witt-vector lift of the defect idempotent q suggests a zero-trace idempotent, but nothing forces a zero-trace idempotent to vanish without positivity (char-0 faithful trace) or an analytic continuation.
lesson.lesson_statement: Lifting coefficients does not import positivity; a zero trace is not a contradiction without a faithful positive trace (K2).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: in char p the Kaplansky trace of an idempotent lies in the prime field (Zalesskii 1972) and carries no positivity; Montgomery 1969 / Kaplansky need a positive faithful trace.
lesson.influence: contributory (start of the positivity clause K2)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: Never formulated as a reason to expect failure of the conjecture in char p.

list.name: Entropy approach: strict entropy decrease on proper linear subshifts (CA/Garden-of-Eden style).
list.obstruction_type: other (nonamenability: naive entropy undefined / not monotone)

lesson.obstruction: Entropy strictly decreasing on proper linear subshifts is a Garden-of-Eden (Moore-Myhill) argument valid for amenable groups; on nonamenable groups naive (Folner) entropy is unavailable.
lesson.lesson_statement: Entropy/dimension counting needs amenability or soficity; it cannot cover arbitrary groups (K3).
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: Garden-of-Eden theorem for amenable groups (Ceccherini-Silberstein-Machi-Scarabotti 1999); failure for nonamenable groups; sofic entropy needs soficity.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The model re-tries entropy/information variants about ten times (secs 5, 7, 8, 9, 10) without treating K3 as a pruning clause.

L1 = strategy, i.e. a commitment to the ANSWER and proof architecture: PROVE (direct finiteness holds; 287's NEG/POS analogue) vs CEX (construct a, b with ab=1, ba!=1). A switch between PROVE and CEX is a RESTART, and each re-entry creates a new L1 node (P1..P5, C1..C5).

L2 = approach family inside a strategy, identified by its central tool or invariant. A summary paragraph that changes the central tool opens a new L2 node. A revisit of an earlier family gets a new node whose clauses_applied point to the earlier lesson.

L3+ = a technical variant, sub-construction or lemma attempted inside an approach. Assign L3 only when the summary presents the step as a refinement of the current approach ('then', 'narrower', 'replaced', 'next').

EXTENSION (197): in the final route, audit sections (13-22) are coded as one L3 node e1.4 whose L4 children are (i) checks that the candidate survives (outcome 'check passed', non-failing, no backtrack), (ii) repairs (outcome 'kept after repair', backtrack with kept_branch_repair=true, as 287's d1.3.3), and (iii) optional strengthenings or replacements that are dropped (Linnik replacement, girth 14, hexagons), coded as ordinary abandoned decisions.

CONFLICT is recorded only where the summary states a failure. A node that fails only because all its children failed is 'abandoned (children failed)' and has no conflict of its own. A node left without a stated reason is 'abandoned (left open)', and its backtrack trigger is 'unclear'.

Backtrack = the next node in trace order is not a child of the current failing node. Distance d = level(failing node) - (level(next node) - 1). d=1 is a sibling; d>=2 is a backjump; next node at L1 is a restart.
Trigger type: conflict if the left node has a stated failure; insight if the left branch was viable but bypassed by a simpler new idea (subsumption); unclear otherwise.

Learned clause = a stated reason for failure phrased as a reusable constraint (or a salvaged tool). Reuse = a later node whose stated reason or design cites or embodies it (explicit if the summary links it, inferred otherwise; see notes).

Length = words of the summary text from the node's first anchor phrase up to the anchor of the next node outside its subtree (page headers and the prompt excerpt excluded; computed at phrase, not line, granularity because several approaches share a line).
Propagation = an explicitly derived consequence or check inside an approach (formula, bound, structural fact), rough count.
